steps.title: Research hub — new Market Phase & Severity Lab tile
steps.narration: The Research hub now includes a Market Phase & Severity Lab tile, visible without scrolling alongside all the existing labs. One click is all it takes to reach the new study.
steps.point_out: The Market Phase & Severity Lab tile with its Thermometer icon in the labs grid. All previously existing tiles — Regime Lab, Factor Lab, and others — remain present and unaffected.

steps.title: Phase & Severity Lab loads with five market-phase rows
steps.narration: Clicking the tile opens a dedicated lab page showing how realized forward returns and paired max-drawdowns have played out across the five market-phase labels — Expansion, Recovery, Pullback, Correction, and Bear — at every standard horizon from 1 to 60 days.
steps.point_out: The by-phase-label table with five rows, one per phase. Cells are colour-graded: positive returns appear in green, negative drawdowns in red. A survivorship-bias caveat is shown above the tables so the descriptive nature of the evidence is always visible.

steps.title: Column sort reorders the phase rows client-side
steps.narration: Clicking any horizon column header sorts the five phase rows by that metric instantly, without a page reload. Rows with too few observations to be reliable always stay at the bottom regardless of sort direction.
steps.point_out: The row order changes after the click — the phase with the highest (or lowest) forward return for that horizon moves to the top. The URL stays the same, confirming the sort is purely client-side.

steps.title: As-of filter restricts evidence to a historical snapshot
steps.narration: Adding an as-of date to the URL scopes both tables to observations that were available on that date. Every N= chip updates to reflect only the qualifying history, making the lab directly usable for walk-forward research.
steps.point_out: The N= chip counts across both tables are noticeably lower than in the all-history view — roughly halved here because data before mid-2024 is excluded. No second date-picker control appears anywhere on the page.

steps.title: N= chip opens a count-matched Samples page for the Bear phase
steps.narration: Every N= chip in the tables is a direct link to the underlying observation list on the Research Samples page. The total shown there always matches the chip exactly — no rounding, no overlap, and the cohort description names both the lab and the market phase you drilled from.
steps.point_out: The Samples page cohort header reads 'Market Phase & Severity Lab' with 'Market phase: Bear' in the slice description, and 'Total observations: 11695' matches the chip number that was clicked.

steps.title: Regime Lab — existing lab is fully intact after the new addition
steps.narration: The Regime Lab introduced in the previous iteration is completely unchanged. Its tables, sort controls, as-of filter, and N= chips all continue to work exactly as before.
steps.point_out: The Regime Lab page loads with its by-regime and by-decile tables populated. No regression from adding the Phase & Severity Lab.

steps.title: Regime Lab drill-through now correctly labels the Samples cohort
steps.narration: A bug fixed in this iteration: Regime Lab N= chips previously landed on a Samples page that showed a generic lab name instead of 'Regime Lab'. The cohort header now correctly identifies where the observations came from, so there is never any ambiguity about which study produced the numbers.
steps.point_out: The Samples page cohort header reads 'Cohort: Regime Lab' — not any other lab name. The observation count still matches the chip that was clicked.
